guides.webhookIntro: Qorva checks {{provider}} for changes every 30 minutes. Add a webhook to have updates arrive as they happen.
guides.webhookManagedOk: Real-time updates are active. Qorva set them up in your ATS — nothing for you to configure.
guides.webhookManagedFailed: Qorva could not set up real-time updates automatically.
guides.pasteSecret: Paste both values into your ATS. It signs every request with the secret, and Qorva ignores anything that does not match.
guides.webhookUrlNotPublic: Your ATS cannot call this address back — it is not publicly reachable over HTTPS. Real-time updates need a public HTTPS address; a local or private one is refused.

greenhouse.intro: You will create a Harvest v3 credential in Greenhouse. You need permission to manage your organisation's API credentials.
steps: In Greenhouse, open Configure → Dev Center → API Credential Management and click Create new API credentials.
Set API type to Harvest v3 (OAuth) and Partner to Unlisted vendor, and describe the credential as Qorva AI.
Create it while signed in as an integration system user rather than a personal account, so the connection keeps working if that person leaves.
Grant read access to candidates, applications, jobs, job posts, users, departments and offices — and nothing beyond that.
Copy the client ID and the client secret, then paste them here. Greenhouse shows the secret only once.
The Greenhouse user ID is optional and only needed if you want Qorva to write match scores back as notes.
greenhouse.note: Harvest v1 and v2 stopped accepting requests on 31 August 2026. An older Harvest API key can no longer connect, so create a Harvest v3 credential even if you already have a key.
webhookSteps: In Greenhouse, open Configure → Dev Center → Web Hooks.
Create a webhook named Qorva AI and choose the candidate event you want to follow.
Paste the address above into Endpoint URL and the secret into Secret Key.
Save it. Greenhouse sends a test call straight away, which Qorva answers for you.
Repeat for each event you want to follow.

recruitee.intro: You need your company ID and a personal API token. The token inherits the permissions of whoever creates it, so use a stable account.
steps: In Recruitee, open Settings → Apps and plugins → API tokens, select the Careers site API tokens tab and turn the toggle on to enable API access.
In Recruitee, open Settings → Apps and plugins → Personal API Tokens and click Add new token.
Name the token Qorva AI and create it.
Copy the token, and note the company ID shown alongside it.
webhookSteps: Check that your Recruitee role has the Manage webhooks ability.
Open Settings → Apps and plugins → Webhooks and click New webhook.
Name it Qorva AI and paste the address above into POST URL.
Select the candidate events you want, click Test, then Verify and create.
Recruitee shows a secret for signing — ignore it. The address above authenticates itself, so there is nothing to paste back into Qorva.

workable.intro: You need an API access token and the subdomain your Workable account uses.
steps: In Workable, open the menu in the top-right corner, choose Integrations, and find the API access tokens section.
Click Generate new token and name it Qorva AI.
Enable the r_jobs and r_candidates scopes. Add w_candidates only if you want Qorva to write match scores back.
Choose an expiry date. Workable tokens expire and syncing stops when they do, so note when you will need to replace it.
Copy the token straight away — Workable shows it in full only once.
Your subdomain is the first part of your Workable address: in https://acme.workable.com it is acme.
workable.webhookUnavailable: Qorva registers Workable's webhook subscriptions over the API — Workable has no webhook screen to fill in by hand.

manatal.intro: You need an Open API token. Manatal includes the Open API on Enterprise Plus; on other plans, ask Manatal to switch it on for you.
steps: In Manatal, open Administration → Features → Open API. If you cannot see it, use Contact our support to request access.
Click Generate new token, name it Qorva AI and generate it.
Copy the token and paste it here. Only Manatal administrators can see API tokens.
manatal.note: If your plan is downgraded or a payment is missed, Manatal deactivates existing tokens and you will need to generate a new one.
webhookSteps: In Manatal, open Administration → Features → Open API and go to the webhooks section.
Add a webhook for candidate events and paste the address above as its destination.
Save it. Contact Manatal support if you need events the screen does not offer.

bamboohr.intro: You need your BambooHR company domain and an API key.
steps: Your company domain is the first part of your BambooHR address: in https://acme.bamboohr.com it is acme.
Sign in with an account that can already see the recruiting data you want Qorva to read — an API key carries exactly that user's permissions.
Click your name in the lower-left corner and choose API Keys.
Add a key, name it Qorva AI, and copy it.
bamboohr.webhookUnavailable: BambooHR webhooks report changes to employee records rather than to applicants, so they cannot drive recruiting updates. Qorva syncs every 30 minutes instead, and you can start a sync at any time.

zoho_recruit.intro: There is nothing to copy for Zoho Recruit. Choose the datacenter your account is hosted in, sign in, and Qorva handles the rest.
steps: Pick the region matching the address you sign in to Zoho with — accounts.zoho.eu means Europe. This is where your account is hosted, not where your company is registered.
Sign in to the Zoho account that holds your Recruit organisation and review the access Qorva asks for.
Click Accept. Zoho sends you back to Qorva and the connection finishes on its own.
webhookSteps: In Zoho Recruit, open Setup → Automation → Actions → Webhooks and click Configure Webhook.
Name it Qorva AI, choose the POST method, and paste the address above into URL to Notify.
Save it, then open Setup → Automation → Workflow Rules and create a rule on the Candidates module.
Choose the record events you want, add the Qorva webhook under Workflow Actions, and activate the rule.
Do not skip the rule: Zoho only sends a webhook that an active workflow rule triggers.

lever.intro: You need an API key. Only a Lever Super Admin can create one.
steps: In Lever, open Settings → Integrations and API and select the API credentials tab.
Under Lever API credentials — not Postings API credentials — click Generate new key.
Name it Qorva AI and grant the read access Qorva needs; selecting all read permissions is the usual choice.
Copy the key and paste it here. Lever shows it only once.
lever.webhookUnavailable: Qorva registers Lever's webhooks over the API. Lever signs them with its own account token, so paste that token here if real-time updates stay inactive.

ashby.intro: You need an API key. Only an Ashby organisation admin can create one.
steps: In Ashby, open Admin → Integrations → API Keys and click New.
Name the key Qorva AI and continue to the permissions screen.
Ashby keys start with no access at all. Grant read access to candidates, jobs, applications, hiring process and organisation data.
Add the apiKeysWrite permission only if you want Qorva to create its webhooks for you later.
Save and copy the key. Ashby will not show it again once the wizard closes.
webhookSteps: In Ashby, open Admin → Integrations → Webhooks and click New.
Choose the event you want to follow.
Paste the address above into the request URL and the secret into the secret token.
Save it. Ashby sends a test call immediately, and the webhook turns itself on once Qorva accepts it.

cycle.year: Billed yearly — limits cover the whole year

plan.purpose: Your plan includes an allowance of AI work for each billing period. Here is how much you have used, what each number counts, and what happens at the limit.

screeningActions.what: One per resume analysed, and one per candidate scored against a job.
screeningActions.details: Counted when a resume is uploaded or imported from your ATS, when a matching run scores a candidate against an open job (only new candidates and changed resumes or jobs — unchanged reports are reused for free — up to the Top N you choose per job), when Data Health re-analyses a resume, and when AI suggests scoring rules.
screeningActions.atLimit: At the limit, uploads, ATS imports, matching and re-analysis pause until the period renews.

aiResumeChats.what: One per Copilot answer about one candidate.
aiResumeChats.details: Each question Copilot answers from a candidate’s full resume, the job and its match report counts once.
aiResumeChats.atLimit: At the limit, Copilot can’t answer questions about a candidate until the period renews.

talentIntelligenceQueries.what: One per Copilot analysis of your whole library.
talentIntelligenceQueries.details: Each library question Copilot answers with counts, charts or candidate cards counts once, follow-ups included.
talentIntelligenceQueries.atLimit: At the limit, Copilot can’t analyse the library until the period renews.

emailTemplates.what: Saved invitation templates — a plan allowance, not reset each period.

agentRuns.what: One per other Copilot request: searching, tagging, drafting, matching, rules.
agentRuns.details: Each task counts once, whether you gave it in chat or a rule started it. Questions about one candidate or the library count on their own meters instead. What Copilot does along the way, such as a matching run, also counts against its own allowance.
agentRuns.atLimit: New Copilot tasks are refused until the period renews; questions about a candidate or the library still work.

pace.WATCH: Close to the limit at this pace

deleteConversation.title: Delete this conversation?
deleteConversation.message: Its tasks and answers will be removed. Nothing Copilot looked at is changed.

empty.title: What should Copilot do?
empty.subtitle: Ask about one candidate or your whole library, or give Copilot a task in plain words. It answers from the full resume, the job and its match report, analyses your library with charts, and can tag candidates, add notes, create or update jobs and draft emails. Sending an email, running matching or an ATS import always waits for your approval. It never deletes anything.

examples.tag: Tag the 3 best-matched candidates for our newest open job as “shortlist”.
examples.skills: What are the most common skills among our senior developers?

input.placeholder: Ask a question or describe a task… Use @ for a candidate, # for a job
input.hint: Copilot reads your data to answer. It can make mistakes, so check important results.

run.failed: Copilot could not finish this task.

run.expired: Expired: an approval was not given in time.

ats.title: Start an ATS import?
ats.note: Runs in the background; each imported resume can use a matching action.

rule.title: Create this rule?
rule.name: Name
rule.note: From now on only: nothing that already exists is processed. You can pause or edit it in Copilot → Rules.

rules.intro: A rule starts a Copilot task by itself when something happens, as you. Emails and other actions still wait for your approval.
rules.empty: No rules yet. Create one, or ask Copilot in the chat: “whenever a candidate scores 80+ on a job, draft an invitation”.
rules.deleteMessage: It stops starting tasks. Tasks it already started are kept in Activity.
